'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Gaza Strip evacuations]]
***[[President of Indonesia|Indonesian President]] [[Prabowo Subianto]] tours the [[Middle East]] to seek support from [[Egypt]], [[Jordan]], [[Qatar]], [[Turkey]], and the [[United Arab Emirates]] for his proposed plan to temporarily evacuate 1,000 [[Palestinians]] from the [[Gaza Strip]] to [[Indonesia]]. [https://indonesiabusinesspost.com/4092/geopolitics-and-diplomacy/indonesia-maintains-gazans-evacuation-plan-as-temporary-selectively-arranged (''Indonesia Business Post'')]
**[[International aid to Palestinians]]
***The [[European Union]] announces a {{Euro}}1.6 billion (US$1.8 billion) three-year [[foreign aid|financial support package]] for [[Palestinians]] aiming to "stabilize" Gaza and the [[West Bank]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/middle-east-eu-pledges-16-billion-for-palestinians/live-72237121 (DW)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[United Kingdom and the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***The [[United Kingdom]] sends [[Pound sterling|£]]752 million ($990 million) to [[Ukraine]] for the purchase of [[surface-to-air missile]]s, [[artillery]] and spare parts for [[fighter aircraft]], as part of an international loan programme funded primarily through seized [[Russia]]n financial assets. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/britain-sends-ukraine-second-part-3-billion-war-loan-2025-04-14/ (Reuters)]
*[[Herder–farmer conflicts in Nigeria]]
**At least 51 people are killed in escalating clashes between rival [[herder]]s in [[Plateau State]], [[Nigeria]], while another 2,000 people are displaced, according to [[Amnesty International]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-51-killed-another-attack-nigerias-plateau-state-2025-04-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Mediterranean Sea migrant smuggling]]
**The [[Hellenic Coast Guard]] finds two bodies and 39 survivors when a boat carrying [[human migration|migrants]] capsizes off the coast of [[Farmakonisi]] in the [[Dodecanese]] islands of [[Greece]]. [https://apnews.com/article/greece-migration-bodies-sinking-9f98a28f960598dd3455c4e42d3fd174 (AP)] [https://greekcitytimes.com/2025/04/15/farmakonisi-migrant-boat/ (''Greek City Times'')]
*A 5.2 [[Richter scale#Richter magnitudes|magnitude]] [[earthquake]] strikes [[Julian, California|Julian]], [[California]], [[United States]]. The earthquake, felt throughout [[Southern California]] and [[Baja California]], caused several rockslides on [[California State Route 76]] and the demolition of an office façade in [[Tecate]], [[Baja California]], [[Mexico]] due to risk of collapse caused by earthquake. [https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2025/04/14/magnitude-5-2-earthquake-near-julian-jolts-san-diego-county-and-beyond/ (''The San Diego Union-Tribune'')] [https://jornadabc.com.mx/bajacalifornia/ante-riesgo-de-colapso-causado-por-el-sismo-demuelen-fachada-de-oficina-de-tecate/ (''La Jornada'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Aging of Japan]]
**According to official data, the population of [[Japanese people|Japanese citizens]] dropped to [[Demographics of Japan|a record low of 120.3 million]] by October 2024, following a 14-year trend of record lows and the largest drop since records began in [[1950 in Japan|1950]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/japan-sees-record-drop-in-population/a-72239612 (DW)] [https://www.stat.go.jp/data/jinsui/new.html (Government of Japan)]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–Vietnam relations]]
**[[China]] and [[Vietnam]] sign 45 agreements, including deals on [[Rail transport in Vietnam|rail links]] and [[supply chain]]s, during [[Paramount leader|Chinese leader]] [[Xi Jinping]]'s [[List of international trips made by Xi Jinping|state visit]] to Vietnam as part of his broader tour across [[Southeast Asia]] in response to tariffs imposed by the United States. Vietnam also approves [[jet aircraft|jet]] purchases from China, with China's [[Comac]] signing a deal with [[Vietjet]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/chinas-xi-meet-vietnam-leaders-kick-off-southeast-asia-tour-amid-us-tariffs-2025-04-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Democratic backsliding in the United States]], [[El Salvador–United States relations]]
**[[U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] suggests deporting United States citizens to the controversial [[Terrorism Confinement Center]] prison in [[El Salvador]], despite the [[Constitution of the United States|unconstitutionality]] of the proposal. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/trump-floats-legally-questionable-proposal-deport-us-citizens-rcna201183 (NBC News)]
*[[July Revolution (Bangladesh)|July Revolution]]
**A court in [[Dhaka]], [[Bangladesh]], along with the [[Anti-Corruption Commission (Bangladesh)|Anti-Corruption Commission]], issues an [[arrest warrant]] for [[Tulip Siddiq]], a [[United Kingdom]] [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|MP]] who is the niece of ousted former [[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|leader]] [[Sheikh Hasina]], for [[corruption]] allegations. Siddiq has rebuked the arrest warrant and called it a "[[smear campaign]]" against her. [https://www.dw.com/en/bangladesh-issues-arrest-warrant-for-uk-mp-linked-to-hasina/a-72235733 (DW)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crm3473wzr0o (BBC News)]
*[[LGBTQ rights in Hungary]]
**The [[Hungarian government]] passes several [[Constitution of Hungary|constitutional]] changes that affect [[LGBTQ rights]], including a provisional law that says [[Hungarians|people]] can only be [[gender binary|male or female]] and [[codification (law)|codify]]ing a law that bans [[LGBTQ events]], including [[Budapest Pride]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/hungary-passes-constitutional-changes-targeting-lgbtq-rights/a-72242414 (DW)]
*The [[Civil Guard (Spain)|Spanish Civil Guard]] arrests two [[Russians|Russian citizens]] in [[Manacor]], [[Mallorca]], for alleged [[animal breeding|breeding]] and [[wildlife smuggling|sale]] of [[exotic felids as pets|exotic cats]], and recover a [[caracal]], two [[serval]]s, and sixteen [[felid hybrid]]s. [https://www.dw.com/en/spanish-police-pounce-on-exotic-cat-smuggling-ring/a-72243276 (DW)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Blue Origin NS-31]]
**A [[Blue Origin]] [[New Shepard]] [[launch vehicle]] makes a brief [[sub-orbital spaceflight]], carrying six female [[space tourism|space tourists]], marking the first all-female spacecraft since 1963's [[Vostok 6]] which had [[Valentina Tereshkova]] as the pilot and the spacecraft's sole passenger. [https://www.npr.org/2025/04/14/nx-s1-5364460/blue-origin-launch-female-space-flight-katy-perry (NPR)] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/celebrities/2025/04/14/katy-perry-gayle-king-lauren-sanchez-blue-origin-space/83046482007/ (USA Today)]
